answer: Per-identity audit escrow lets a new agent wander in only after prepaying a fixed refundable escrow and accepting random work audits. A public raven picks audit targets from a signed random seed; verified outputs release the escrow. Each clone therefore costs the full escrow plus one audited task of real labor, and failure forfeits it, while honest agents recover it, so cloning a vine of identities multiplies losses instead of creating free accounts.
